# Developer Testing Guide: Recorded Video Camera

**Branch**: `feature/recorded-video-camera` | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) | **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md)

**Purpose**: Step-by-step guide for the developer to verify the feature after implementation. Generated by `/speckit-plan` and finalized by `/speckit-implement` (T074) against the built tool. Reference the spec, contracts and data model rather than duplicating them. No full test code here.

Status: finalized. Output text below is what the tool prints (captured 2026-11-11 with a fresh
`TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME`). One item is still open: the ghosting threshold is the research value
`GHOST_THRESHOLD = 40` in `src/teams_avatar/analysis.py`, tuned in TS-015 (T071) on 2026-11-12.
TS-001 (Teams) passed on 2026-11-12; TS-002 (Zoom) has not been run yet (see section 8).

## 1. Prerequisites

- [ ] Dependencies installed from the lock file: `uv sync`
- [ ] Devices and components available: a physical webcam; OBS Studio installed with its virtual
      camera **not** started in OBS; Teams desktop and Zoom desktop installed; ffmpeg on `PATH`
      (test tool only, for capture measurements)
- [ ] Settings needed: a clean data folder for the run — `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME = "$env:TEMP\ta-test"`
      (remove it first) so the first-use notice and defaults are exercised
- [ ] Sample or fixture data (create a folder first: `$d = "$env:TEMP\ta-clips"; mkdir $d`). The
      counter clips come from `tests/clips.py` `write_clip(path, frames, width, height, fps=30,
      distinct=True)`; each frame carries its own number, so `tools.frame_check` can spot repeats.
      Run each line from the repo root:
  - `bar-clip.mp4` (30 s, 1280×720, every frame different):
    `uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; from tests.clips import write_clip; write_clip(Path('$d/bar-clip.mp4'), 900, 1280, 720)"`
  - `short.mp4` (3 s, too short to blend): same, with `90, 1280, 720`
  - `ghost.mp4` (10 s, first and last frames differ): same, with `300, 1280, 720`
  - `portrait.mp4` (5 s, 1080×1920): same, with `150, 1080, 1920`
  - `big.mp4` (3 s, 3840×2160): same, with `90, 3840, 2160`
  - `still.mp4` (10 s, identical frames, imports with no ghosting warning): same, with `300, 1280, 720, distinct=False`
  - `not-video.mp4`: `"hello" | Set-Content $d\not-video.mp4`
  - `truncated.mp4`: `$b = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("$d\bar-clip.mp4"); [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("$d\truncated.mp4", $b[0..($b.Length/2)])`
  - Alternative for a clip with ffmpeg: `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\bin\ffmpeg.exe -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 -t 30 -pix_fmt yuv420p bar-clip.mp4`
  - Note: every counter clip except `still.mp4` imports with the ghosting warning, because its
    background brightness changes with the frame number. That is expected, not a defect.

## 2. Automated checks

Run these first; all must pass before manual testing.

| Check | Command | Expected |
|-------|---------|----------|
| Type check | `uv run mypy src tests tools` | No errors |
| Lint | `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` | No errors |
| Pytest (focused) | `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_loop_player.py` | All pass |
| Pytest (full, no hardware) | `uv run pytest` | All pass; hardware tests skipped with reason "needs camera/OBS; set TEAMS_AVATAR_HW=1" |
| Pytest (hardware) | `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HW=1; uv run pytest tests/contract` | All pass (camera free and well lit, OBS virtual camera not in use) |
| Frame check (test tool) | `uv run python -m tools.frame_check capture.framemd5 --seconds 600` | One line such as `received 18001/18000, repeated 0, dropped 0 -> 0.00% bad (target <= 1%)`; exit 0 (1 if over 1%) |

### Recorded results (T070, development machine, 2026-11-11)

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26220, Python 3.12.1, OBS Studio 32.0.4, "Integrated Camera" (yuyv422 only),
plus a Kyocera ECOSYS M3645idn scanner that Windows lists in the Image class.

| Run | Result |
|-----|--------|
| `uv run pytest` | 332 passed, 6 skipped (hardware) |
| `uv run mypy src tests tools` / `uv run ruff check .` | clean / clean |
| `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HW=1; uv run pytest tests/contract` | 33 passed, 3 failed |

- Passed on hardware: every OBS Virtual Camera contract (90 frames at 720p, second sender →
  `in_use`, missing OBS → `not_installed`), the codec and the named-pipe contracts.
- Failed on hardware: the three `test_camera_hw.py` tests. The Integrated Camera delivered 7–10
  frames per second in every mode with a nearly black picture (mean brightness 13–16 of 255): the
  room was dark or the privacy shutter closed. The tool refused as designed, within 6 s:
  `error: The camera "Integrated Camera" cannot be used: it is unusable for recording: it only
  delivers 10 frames per second, usually because the room is too dark or the camera shutter is
  closed. Add light or open the camera shutter, then try again.`
  **Re-run in normal light before sign-off**; R2's probe measured 30 fps at 1280×720.
- `teams-avatar cameras` also lists the scanner (Windows puts it in the Image class, as R2
  expected); `record --camera` on it is refused as unusable.

### Recorded results (T048, presentation path, development machine, 2026-11-11)

OBS Studio 32.0.4, 1280×720 counter and gradient clips, no meeting app.

| Measure | Result | Target |
|---------|--------|--------|
| `present` from cold (SC-002) | 1.0–1.3 s | ≤ 30 s |
| Service CPU (SC-007) | 0.13–0.14 of one core | ≤ 0.25 |
| 10-minute consumer capture (SC-004) | 18001/18000 received, 0 repeated, 0 dropped = 0.00% | ≤ 1% |
| `stop` to placeholder (SC-005) | 10/10 within limit, max 569 ms from the start of the `stop` command | ≤ 2 s |

A blind critic judged our blended repeat less noticeable than OBS's own Media Source loop, which
hard-cuts. Our remaining tell is a visible 1 s double exposure mid-blend every (N − 30) frames
(N = frames in the clip).

## 3. Manual test scenarios

Run TS-007 to TS-009 in normal light: in a dark room or with the shutter closed the camera
delivers 7–10 fps and `record` refuses it (see section 5).

### TS-001: Present a recording in Teams (User Story 1, scenario 1; FR-006)

- **Preconditions**: Library contains `bar-clip` (imported); Teams running.
- **Steps**:
  1. `uv run teams-avatar present bar-clip`
  2. In Teams → Settings → Devices, choose "OBS Virtual Camera".
- **Expected result**: `present` prints `Presenting "bar-clip" (recording 1280x720) on OBS Virtual
  Camera, canvas 1280x720 at 30 fps.` (canvas 1920x1080 after `quality 1080p`), `Recording
  indicator: OFF`, `In Teams or Zoom, choose "OBS Virtual Camera" as your camera.`, `If it is not
  listed, close and reopen Teams or Zoom, or reopen its camera settings.`, `Keep the "Teams
  Avatar" window open during meetings; closing it stops the camera.`, then one `Warning:` line
  per recording warning. Teams preview shows the clip. Command returned within 30 s (SC-002).
- **Note**: This is the plan's biggest open risk (R1): whether Teams lists the camera while
  pyvirtualcam drives it. Run it before anything else; if it fails, revisit R1.
- **Result**: [x] Pass  Notes: 2026-11-12, Teams listed "OBS Virtual Camera" while the tool drove it and showed "Still 1", "Move 1" and "Stand 1" looping. R1 holds.

### TS-002: Present a recording in Zoom (User Story 1, scenario 1; FR-006)

- **Preconditions**: As TS-001, Zoom running.
- **Steps**: With presentation running, Zoom → Settings → Video → Camera → "OBS Virtual Camera".
- **Expected result**: Zoom preview shows the clip. Same open risk as TS-001.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-003: Repeat point blends (User Story 1, scenario 2; FR-007)

- **Preconditions**: Presenting `bar-clip`.
- **Steps**: Watch the Teams preview across at least three repeats.
- **Expected result**: End fades into start over about one second; no blank, frozen or jumping
  picture.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-004: Stop shows the placeholder within 2 s (User Story 1, scenario 3; FR-008, FR-020; SC-005)

- **Steps**:
  1. Watch the Teams preview; `uv run teams-avatar stop`.
  2. Measured: with `bar-clip` presenting, start a capture with wall-clock timestamps,
     `ffmpeg -f dshow -video_size 1280x720 -framerate 30 -i video="OBS Virtual Camera" -use_wallclock_as_timestamps 1 -copyts -frames:v 150 -f framemd5 stop.md5`,
     and note the wall-clock time (Unix seconds) just before `stop` starts. The framemd5 time
     base is 1/30 s, so a line's pts × 1/30 is that frame's wall-clock time. The first placeholder
     frame is the first line after which the hash stays the same (the counter frames stop
     changing). Latency = that frame's pts / 30 − the time `stop` started. Repeat 10 times
     (`present bar-clip` again each time).
- **Expected result**: `stop` prints `Stopped. The camera now shows "Camera paused".` (when not
  presenting: `Not presenting; nothing to stop.`, exit 0). Placeholder within 2 s in all 10 runs
  (dev machine: max 569 ms); you can then choose your real camera in Teams.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-005: Status while presenting (User Story 1, scenario 4; FR-009)

- **Steps**: While presenting, `uv run teams-avatar status`.
- **Expected result**: `Presenting "bar-clip" for 0:00:42. Canvas 1280x720 (quality 720p).
  Recording indicator: OFF` with the elapsed time increasing between two calls. When not
  presenting: `Not presenting; the camera shows "Camera paused". Canvas 1280x720 (quality 720p).
  Recording indicator: OFF`. Service not running: `The camera service is not running. Quality
  720p. Recording indicator: OFF`. `status --json` gives the same facts as fields.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-006: Indicator off by default, switchable, state always visible (User Story 1, scenario 5; FR-017; Principle I)

- **Steps**: Present; confirm no banner. `indicator on`; then `indicator off`. Each time, hover the
  taskbar button of the "Teams Avatar" service window.
- **Expected result**: No banner by default; `indicator on` prints `Recording indicator: ON` and
  the banner "RECORDED VIDEO" appears within 1 s; `indicator off` prints `Recording indicator:
  OFF` and it disappears; `status` and the service window title reflect each state.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-007: Record with preview (User Story 2, scenarios 1–2; FR-001, FR-003, FR-004)

- **Preconditions**: Normal light; camera free.
- **Steps**: `uv run teams-avatar record`; check the preview window; record ~20 s; press `Space`.
- **Expected result**: Live preview with "REC" and elapsed time; prints `Saved "Recording
  YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS": 0:00:20, 1280x720, 30 fps.` (plus any `Warning:` line); appears in
  `list` with origin `recorded`; still there after reboot/restart of the tool.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-008: Cancel recording (User Story 2, scenario 3; FR-003)

- **Preconditions**: Normal light.
- **Steps**: `record --name Cancelme`; after 5 s press `Esc`.
- **Expected result**: Prints `Cancelled; nothing was saved.`, exit 0; nothing in `list`; no `*.partial.mp4` left in the recordings folder.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-009: Choose a camera (User Story 2, scenario 4; FR-002)

- **Preconditions**: Normal light; a second physical camera connected (skip with a note if none).
- **Steps**: `cameras`; `record --camera "<second camera>"`.
- **Expected result**: One name per line, the first marked `(default)` (for example
  `Integrated Camera (default)`); "OBS Virtual Camera" not listed; preview shows the chosen
  camera. Windows may also list Image-class devices that are not cameras, such as the Kyocera
  scanner on the development machine; choosing one is refused as unusable. With no camera:
  `No camera found. Connect a camera, then try again.`
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail [ ] Skipped (no second camera)  Notes:

### TS-010: List, preview, rename, default, delete (User Story 3; FR-005)

- **Preconditions**: Three recordings.
- **Steps**: `list`; `preview <one>`; `rename <one> "New name"`; `default <two>`;
  `delete <three>` (answer `y`); `present` with no name.
- **Expected result**: `list` prints a table with columns `Name  Duration  Added  Size  Picture
  Origin  Notes` (notes: `default`, `presenting`, `missing`, `too short`, `may ghost at repeat`);
  `rename` prints `Renamed to "New name".`; `default` prints `"<two>" is now the default
  recording.`; `delete` asks `Delete "<three>" and its video file? [y/N]` then prints
  `Deleted "<three>".` and the file is gone from disk (`--yes` skips the question); `present` with
  no name presents the default. With no default and no name: `error: No recording name was given
  and no default recording is set. Name a recording, or set one with "teams-avatar default
  <recording>".`
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-011: Import a file (FR-021, FR-022)

- **Steps**: `import bar-clip.mp4`; `import portrait.mp4`; `import big.mp4`.
- **Expected result**: Each prints `Imported "<name>": 0:00:30, 1280x720, 30 fps.` (the name
  defaults to the date and time; use `--name`); originals unchanged (compare hashes
  before/after); `big` is reported and stored at no more than `1920x1080`; `portrait` stays portrait and, when presented, sits inside the frame on the
  neutral background without being enlarged.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-012: Presentation quality setting (FR-023)

- **Steps**: `quality 1080p`; `shutdown`; present a 1080p recording; `stop`; present a 720p
  recording. `quality` prints `Presentation quality set to 1080p. It applies the next time you
  present.`; if the camera service is already running it adds `The camera is already running at
  the old size. Run "teams-avatar shutdown", then "teams-avatar present" to use it.` `shutdown`
  prints `Released OBS Virtual Camera; the Teams Avatar window has closed.` (or `Nothing to
  release; the camera is not running.`). A value other than `720p` or `1080p` is a usage error
  (exit 2).
- **Expected result**: `status` shows quality 1080p and canvas 1920×1080 for both; the 1080p
  recording fills the frame; the 720p recording is shown at its own size, centred with a neutral
  border (not enlarged). Teams did not need the camera re-selected between them. Ask the user
  whether the bordered 720p look is acceptable (plan risk).
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-013: First-use notice (Principle I)

- **Steps**: With a clean data folder, run any command.
- **Expected result**: Notice begins `Teams Avatar shows a recording of you in place of your live
  camera.`, says the "RECORDED VIDEO" indicator is off by default and that you are responsible
  for telling participants and following your organisation's and meeting hosts' rules, and ends
  `Type y to continue: `; not shown again. With a clean folder, `list --json` prints `error: The
  first-use notice has not been accepted. Run the command in a terminal and type y, or add
  --accept-notice.` and a JSON `error` object that includes the notice, exit code 3; with
  `--accept-notice` it succeeds (`No recordings yet. Run "teams-avatar record" or "teams-avatar
  import <file>".`).
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-014: First-time user reaches a meeting in under 5 minutes (SC-001)

- **Preconditions**: Tool and OBS Studio installed (plan's SC-001 interpretation); clean data
  folder; Teams open.
- **Steps**: Start a stopwatch; acknowledge notice; `record` ~20 s; `present`; select
  "OBS Virtual Camera" in Teams; stop the watch when the recording shows in Teams' preview.
- **Expected result**: Under 5 minutes.
- **Result**: [ ] Pass [ ] Fail  Notes:

### TS-015: Tune the ghosting threshold (T071; research R5)

- **Preconditions**: Normal light; the threshold in `src/teams_avatar/analysis.py` is still the
  research value `GHOST_THRESHOLD = 12`.
- **Steps**:
  1. Record three clips of about 10 s with `record`: (a) sitting still; (b) small movement (head
     turn, hand gesture) returning to roughly the same pose; (c) sitting at the start and
     standing at the end.
  2. Score each one's first and last frame (replace `<file>` with its path under `recordings\`):
     `uv run python -c "import av; from teams_avatar.analysis import ghost_score; f=[x.to_ndarray(format='bgr24') for x in av.open(r'<file>').decode(video=0)]; print(round(ghost_score(f[0], f[-1]), 1))"`
  3. Present each and watch the repeat in the Teams preview; note which are fine and which show a
     visible double image.
  4. Pick a threshold between the highest "fine" score and the lowest "visible ghost" score, set
     `GHOST_THRESHOLD` to it, and record the three scores and the choice in `research.md` R5.
  5. Run `uv run pytest`, then confirm `import` warns for the clip that ghosts and not for the
     others.
- **Expected result**: The still and small-movement clips score below the threshold; the sitting
  vs standing clip scores above it.
- **Result**: [x] Pass (with a change to the plan)  Scores: still 8.5, small 7.3, sit/stand 39.3
  Chosen: 40. Run 2026-11-12 in Teams: none of the three showed a double image, including
  sit/stand, so the expectation that it scores above the threshold was revised: the threshold
  sits just above the highest score seen to be fine. See research.md R5.

## 4. Safety and privacy checks

| Rule | How to check | Expected |
|------|--------------|----------|
| Live camera never reaches a meeting through the tool (FR-011, SC-006) | While presenting, look at the webcam's in-use light and Windows' camera privacy indicator; also during `stop` and after a forced failure | Light off and no app listed as using the camera, in every state of the camera service |
| No network connections (FR-012, Principle I) | Run `record`, `import`, `present`, `stop` while watching `Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess <pid>` and `Get-NetUDPEndpoint` for the tool's processes | No entries for any tool process |
| Logs and activity contain no picture content (FR-016, Principle IV) | Inspect `logs\teams-avatar.log` and `activity.jsonl` | Text only; no image data; each line has a `session_id` where applicable |
| Data stays in the user's folder (FR-012) | List files changed during the run outside `TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` | Only the folder itself |
| Indicator state always visible while presenting (Principle I) | Service window title on the taskbar for the whole presentation; `present` output; `status` | All three state ON/OFF and agree |
| Pipe accepts only the right key | Connect to the pipe with a wrong key (hardware-free contract test covers this) | Rejected |

## 5. Edge cases and error paths

| Case | How to trigger | Expected |
|------|----------------|----------|
| Camera too dark or shutter closed (dev machine: 7–10 fps) | Cover the lens or use a dark room, then `record` | Exit 1, within about 6 s, no recording or partial file: `error: The camera "Integrated Camera" cannot be used: it is unusable for recording: it only delivers 10 frames per second, usually because the room is too dark or the camera shutter is closed. Add light or open the camera shutter, then try again.` |
| Scanner or other non-camera device listed by `cameras` | `record --camera "<scanner name>"` | Refused as unusable (exit 1) |
| Camera in use by another app | Open Windows Camera app, then `record` | Plain message naming the cause (exit 1); no recording or partial file created |
| Storage runs out while recording | Point `TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` at a small VHD/USB stick (~300 MB) and record until full | Recording stops with a message; what was recorded is kept as a valid, playable recording |
| Present while already presenting | `present a` then `present b`; then `present a` again | `b` refused: `error: "a" is already being presented. …` (exit code 3); repeating `a` prints status, exit 0 |
| Recording file missing | Delete `recordings\<id>.mp4` by hand; `list`; `present` it | `list` marks it `missing`; `present` names the recording and presents nothing |
| Recording becomes unreadable mid-presentation | Present, then overwrite the file with garbage | Camera switches to placeholder; service window shows the failure; `status` shows not presenting; activity records `failed` |
| Decoder stalls (unit-tested with a fake that blocks) | `uv run pytest -k stall` | Placeholder sent within 200 ms of the last frame; presentation `failed` |
| Tool closed/crashes during a meeting | (a) `shutdown`; (b) close the service window; (c) end the service process in Task Manager — each while Teams shows the camera | Teams shows OBS's placeholder or no video; never the live camera and never a frozen frame of the recording; record what each case shows (plan risk) |
| Interrupted writes recovered | Kill `record` mid-recording; separately delete a recording's entry from `library.json` by hand; run `list` | No `*.partial.mp4` left; the orphaned file is listed as `Recovered …` and reported once |
| Two `present` commands at once | Run `present a` in two terminals at the same moment with no service running | One service starts; one command presents, the other reports success (same recording) or refusal (different) |
| Too-short recording | `import short.mp4` | Saved with `Warning: it is shorter than 5 seconds, so it repeats without a blend.`; repeats plainly when presented |
| Start/end differ strongly | `import ghost.mp4` | Saved with `Warning: its first and last moments differ a lot, so the 1-second blend may show a double image.`; `list` notes `may ghost at repeat` |
| Meeting app opened before presentation does not list the camera | Start Teams first, then `present` | `present` output tells the user how to make the camera appear (restart the app or reselect) |
| Delete while presenting | `delete <presenting recording> --yes` | Refused (exit code 3) until `stop`: `error: "<name>" is being presented. Run "teams-avatar stop" first, then delete it.` |
| Delete without a terminal or `--yes` | `delete <name>` with piped stdin, or with `--json` | `error: Deleting "<name>" was cancelled. Run the command in a terminal and type y, or add --yes.` exit 3; recording kept |
| Unknown recording | `delete nope --yes` | `error: No recording matches "nope". Run "teams-avatar list" to see names, or give at least 6 characters of its id.` exit 1 |
| Name clash | `import bar-clip.mp4 --name "Test 1"` when "Test 1" exists | `error: A recording named "Test 1" already exists. Choose another name.` exit 3; existing recording untouched |
| Not a video / damaged / missing file | `import not-video.mp4`, `import truncated.mp4`, `import nothere.mp4` | `error: "not-video.mp4" was not imported: the file is not a valid or complete video. Choose a playable video file (for example MP4) and try again.` (missing file: `the file does not exist`), exit 1; library unchanged; `history` shows `import_rejected` |
| OBS virtual camera started inside OBS | Start it in OBS, then `present` | Message to stop OBS's virtual camera (exit code 4) |
| OBS not installed | Run on a machine/VM without OBS | Message with install guidance (exit code 4) |

## 6. Data verification

| What this proves | How to check | Expected |
|------------------|--------------|----------|
| Recording stored with correct details (FR-004) | `list --json` vs `ffprobe` on `recordings\<id>.mp4` | Duration, size, picture size and 30 fps match |
| Partial files cleaned up (FR-003) | `Get-ChildItem recordings\*.partial.mp4` after cancel/failure | None |
| Default is single (data model) | `library.json` | At most one `is_default: true` |
| Activity record written (FR-016) | `history` and `activity.jsonl` | One line per record, import, presentation start/end, rename, delete, failure |
| Settings persisted (FR-017, FR-023) | Change indicator and quality; `shutdown`; `present`; `status` | `status` shows the saved indicator state and quality setting after the restart |
| History output | `history --limit 6` | Lines like `2026-11-11 21:19:45  renamed "Short one": renamed - Renamed from "short".`; empty: `No activity yet.` |
| Schema version present (research R8) | Open `library.json`, `settings.json` | Each has `"schema_version": 1` |

## 7. Regression and non-functional checks

- [ ] Adjacent features still work: n/a for the first feature; confirm OBS Studio's own virtual
      camera still works after `shutdown`
- [ ] Performance expectation from plan:
  - Quality Bar: present `bar-clip` and capture 10 minutes with
    `ffmpeg -f dshow -video_size 1280x720 -framerate 30 -i video="OBS Virtual Camera" -t 600 -f framemd5 out.md5`;
    then `uv run python -m tools.frame_check out.md5 --seconds 600` counts consecutive identical
    hashes and missing frames: ≤ 1% combined (SC-004). It ignores the one start-up duplicate
    that DirectShow produces (`--keep-start-duplicate` counts it). Dev machine: 18001/18000, 0.00%.
  - Same clip through OBS Studio (Media Source, Loop on, virtual camera at 720p30) and through the
    tool, 60 s capture each spanning the repeat point; compare side by side (Quality Bar question)
  - CPU while presenting at 720p: `(Get-Process -Id <service pid>).CPU` read twice 60 s apart;
    difference ÷ 60 ≤ 0.25 (25% of one core, SC-007 target from plan). Do not use Task Manager's
    percentage, which is a share of all cores.
  - 2-hour presentation in a real or test meeting with a second participant: no blank, frozen or
    stuttering picture (SC-003)
- [ ] Cleanup: `teams-avatar shutdown`; remove `$env:TEAMS_AVATAR_HOME` test folder; unset
      `TEAMS_AVATAR_HW`
